name: log
title: Log Data
description: Prints data from the routed message (such as body and headers) to the logger.
label: core,monitoring

properties.name: loggerName
properties.description: Name of the logging category to use

properties.name: groupActiveOnly
properties.description: If true, will hide stats when no new messages have been received for a time interval, if false, show stats regardless of message traffic.

properties.name: groupDelay
properties.description: Set the initial delay for stats (in millis)

properties.name: groupInterval
properties.description: If specified will group message stats by this time interval (in millis)

properties.name: groupSize
properties.description: An integer that specifies a group size for throughput logging.

properties.name: level
properties.description: Logging level to use. The default value is INFO.

properties.name: logMask
properties.description: If true, mask sensitive information like password or passphrase in the log.

properties.name: marker
properties.description: An optional Marker name to use.

properties.name: plain
properties.description: If enabled only the body will be printed out

properties.name: sourceLocationLoggerName
properties.description: If enabled then the source location of where the log endpoint is used in Camel routes, would be used as logger name, instead of the given name. However, if the source location is disabled or not possible to resolve then the existing logger name will be used.

properties.name: lazyStartProducer
properties.label: producer,advanced
properties.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

properties.name: exchangeFormatter
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: To use a custom exchange formatter

properties.name: maxChars
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: Limits the number of characters logged per line.

properties.name: multiline
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: If enabled then each information is outputted on a newline.

properties.name: showAll
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: Quick option for turning all options on. (multiline, maxChars has to be manually set if to be used)

properties.name: showAllProperties
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: Show all of the exchange properties (both internal and custom).

properties.name: showBody
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: Show the message body.

properties.name: showBodyType
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: Show the body Java type.

properties.name: showCachedStreams
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: Whether Camel should show cached stream bodies or not (org.apache.camel.StreamCache).

properties.name: showCaughtException
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: If the exchange has a caught exception, show the exception message (no stack trace). A caught exception is stored as a property on the exchange (using the key org.apache.camel.Exchange#EXCEPTION_CAUGHT) and for instance a doCatch can catch exceptions.

properties.name: showException
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: If the exchange has an exception, show the exception message (no stacktrace)

properties.name: showExchangeId
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: Show the unique exchange ID.

properties.name: showExchangePattern
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: Shows the Message Exchange Pattern (or MEP for short).

properties.name: showFiles
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: If enabled Camel will output files

properties.name: showFuture
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: If enabled Camel will on Future objects wait for it to complete to obtain the payload to be logged.

properties.name: showHeaders
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: Show the message headers.

properties.name: showProperties
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: Show the exchange properties (only custom). Use showAllProperties to show both internal and custom properties.

properties.name: showRouteGroup
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: Show route Group.

properties.name: showRouteId
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: Show route ID.

properties.name: showStackTrace
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: Show the stack trace, if an exchange has an exception. Only effective if one of showAll, showException or showCaughtException are enabled.

properties.name: showStreams
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: Whether Camel should show stream bodies or not (eg such as java.io.InputStream). Beware if you enable this option then you may not be able later to access the message body as the stream have already been read by this logger. To remedy this you will have to use Stream Caching.

properties.name: showVariables
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: Show the variables.

properties.name: skipBodyLineSeparator
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: Whether to skip line separators when logging the message body. This allows to log the message body in one line, setting this option to false will preserve any line separators from the body, which then will log the body as is.

properties.name: style
properties.label: formatting
properties.description: Sets the outputs style to use.
